evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 18: in eā prōvinciā pecūniās magnās conlocātās habent
terms.comment: Latin says it with the verb: pecūniam collocāre, to invest money; to invest in a farm, in fundō collocāre (Cic. Caecin. 11, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 2.87: dē quaerendā, dē collocandā pecūniā
Cic. Caecin. 15: nusquam posse eam melius conlocārī

terms.comment: Traupman’s noun; classically collocātiō is a placing or arrangement, or the giving of a daughter in marriage (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: dē quaerendā, dē collocandā pecūniā (vellem etiam dē ūtendā)
phrases.english: on how to make money and how to invest it (I wish also on how to use it)
it could not be better invested anywhere

sources: Lewis & Short: colloco · Lewis & Short: collocatio · Lewis & Short: pecunia
